# Helix inside T3 Code

Use this path only inside T3 with its orchestration tools available. T3 owns
provider integration, discovery, delegation and durable task state. Helix supplies
the implementation, verification, independent-review and correction procedure.
Do not add a runtime, adapter, service, token reader or private HTTP client.
If T3 tools are absent, use the current host's supported [dispatch route](dispatch.md);
if the task specifically requires T3 or cross-provider execution, keep that
requirement blocked rather than silently substituting native delegation.

## Resolve the actual targets

Call `orchestrator_capabilities` and inspect the live tool schemas before dispatch.
Use its inherited provider/model, configured provider instances, model IDs,
model-specific option descriptors, runtime modes, constraints and
`canRunChildTask` / `canRunCrossProviderChildTask` flags. Do not maintain a model
list or map vendor options yourself. If the live schema offers a broader
catalog view, such as all models rather than favorites, request it for choices
and disclose any filter or omitted count the response reports. Catalog
availability is not successful authentication or execution proof. Do not
inspect or export credentials.

Honor explicit writer/reviewer provider, literal model and reasoning effort.
Resolve effort through that model's advertised option ID and values, then pass
`target.options` in the supported shape, such as `[{id, value}]`. Do not assume
every provider calls the option `effort`, or that `xhigh` exists for every model.
For cross-provider work, set `target.providerInstanceId`; set `target.model` only
for an explicit request or applicable saved preference for that provider/driver. Otherwise omit the model
and report T3's returned choice. Requested effort without a resolved model needs
clarification or an unresolved-setting report, not guessed option descriptors.
Do not dispatch that target while a requested setting remains unresolved.
Different account instances of the same provider do not establish a
different-provider review; compare the advertised driver/provider identity too.
A missing or disabled provider and unsupported or ambiguous options need a
concrete limitation or clarification, never a substitute. T3's visible catalog
can omit models hidden in provider settings or excluded by another reported
filter. A missing model is therefore "not advertised, possibly filtered", not
proved unsupported. Preserve an explicit
literal model and let T3 validate it; if its effort descriptors are unavailable,
resolve them through supported T3 metadata or report that setting unresolved.
Never guess option IDs. Show the full returned catalog and disclose its visibility
filter; do not reconstruct a private catalog or silently unhide models.
For unspecified choices, preserve applicable host defaults. On another provider,
T3's default comes from its internal model list, which may differ from the visible
catalog. Report the model returned by dispatch rather than predicting that default.
Options inherit only when the same provider instance and model are kept and
no options are passed.

T3 delegation does not select Claude's named `helix-reviewer` role or Codex's
native `[agents]` defaults. Do not call inherited writer settings saved reviewer
preferences, or claim native role tool limits apply to a T3 child. If existing
reviewer preferences are relevant, disclose this boundary and honor their exact
model/effort through supported T3 targets, with per-task requests taking priority.
Disclose native role tool limits that T3 cannot apply; a saved native tool list
alone does not establish an enforced-isolation requirement for T3. If explicit
user or repository isolation requirements, or the requested model/effort, cannot
be applied, report the reviewer unavailable rather than silently dropping them.
Unspecified choices may use T3's
inherited defaults, clearly labeled. Outside T3, native roles remain unchanged.

The current session is normally the writer. If requested writer settings differ
and T3 can apply them, use one `delegate_task` with `role: implementation` and the
exact target. Give that writer the task, repository rules, allowed scope and
verification requirements. Ask it to return the complete delta and captured
verification output; keep independent review with the coordinator. Do not edit
alongside it. Apply the same single-writer rule to subsequent corrections.

## Independent review and correction

Use `delegate_task` with `role: review` for one fresh reviewer. T3 creates a new
child from the supplied task, without copying the parent's conversation. Include
the actual Helix review brief, requirements, baseline, repository rules, full
final delta (staged, unstaged and new files), captured verification output and
known gaps. Supply full text, or readable artifacts inside the task's
write scope, not only filenames the child cannot access. Do not transfer
private reasoning or the writer's conversation.
Pause edits while the reviewer examines this frozen state. Keep the default
`isolation: shared` for a reviewer that reads the working tree; a `worktree`
child starts from the parent's last commit without uncommitted edits, so it
needs the full delta as text.

`role: review` is a prompt label, not a permission boundary. Use the host's
available read-only tools or sandbox without broadening the caller's authority.
A narrower runtime or interaction mode is not a read-only switch. Leave the
runtime mode inherited unless the user asks otherwise. Inheritance uses the
parent's mode, stepped down to what the target provider offers, and can fall
back to `approval-required`; compare the parent's `runtimeMode` with the
target's advertised `runtimeModes` in the capabilities response. A supervised
child usually pauses for approvals the parent cannot give, so tell the user
approvals may be needed in the child's thread. State which controls actually
apply and any remaining enforcement gap; do not invent a read-only T3 mode. If the task
requires enforced isolation that cannot be provided, stop that dispatch and
continue other authorized work. A copied checkout does not enforce isolation.

Delegation requires an active parent run owned by the current T3 MCP session;
an idle thread or standalone client is not a substitute. A null
`parentThreadId` in the capabilities response means this session is not inside
a T3 thread; use the direct-host workflow.
Track each result by `taskId`, `childThreadId` and `childRunId`. `mode: wait` can
time out without cancelling the child; retain the task ID and use `task_status`
instead of duplicating the task. For async work, follow the current tool's wake
contract and use status for timeout/recovery, not a busy polling loop.
Reading a terminal result through `task_status` or a complete thread read
consumes its notification; do not then wait for a wake. Use `task_cancel` only
when cancellation is intended. Inspect `workState`, pending
child runs, terminal status and returned evidence; `completed` does not prove a
passing check, an independent review or approval. Read truncated results through
the supported thread-read pagination/text offsets or obtain readable artifacts;
a truncated read is not the complete result.

After corrections, rerun affected checks and required gates. **Every new T3
review round is a new `delegate_task` call**, with the original brief, complete
revised delta, fresh verification output, prior findings, responses and unresolved
objections. Give each round a distinct `clientRequestId`, stable only when retrying
that same round. Messaging a completed child's `childThreadId` with
`t3_thread_send` does not reopen the old task or replace its published result.
T3's thread-send tool can return a fresh follow-up `taskId` while reusing the
child's provider conversation. That is not a fresh independent review; do not
use it for Helix review rounds. T3's design document says there is no
task-level follow-up API and omits this thread-send follow-up; the tool schema
and description document it and take precedence. Helix's correction loop and
completion requirements remain unchanged.

## Evidence and current boundary

Record requested and observed provider instance/driver, model, option selections,
task/run IDs, result and enforcement controls, without account data or tokens.
T3's task result reports provider/model, and thread configuration, where
exposed, shows the requested selection; verify effort against correlated native execution records
when exposed. T3 skips option validation for models without descriptors, so an
accepted option is not proof it applied. Requested options and model
self-reports alone do not prove effective effort. Mark unexposed settings
unverified.
